title: Milky Way Across the Desert
caption: The Milky Way over the Atacama Desert from Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This panorama of the Atacama Desert frames a sweeping view of our Milky Way, seen with great clarity because this remote area has minimal light pollution. Huge interstellar dust clouds block the light of more distant stars, giving the band its characteristic mottled look.

ESO photo ambassador Petr Horálek captured the scene in 2019 from the top of Cerro Armazones, where the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) is being built. The mountain rises to 3046 meters in the heart of the Atacama, and its height and dryness will be vital for putting the ELT's observing power to full use.
Picking a site for a new telescope is done with great care, so that it offers the best possible observing conditions. Views like this one show what Cerro Armazones has to offer.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based panoramic photograph by Petr Horálek. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A panorama takes in more of the sky than the eye can at once, and a camera gathering light over time may show the Milky Way's dust more clearly too.

alt: A wide panorama of desert under the Milky Way, whose bright band is broken by dark dust clouds.
